clue.text: Territory bordering a pole, oddly?

indicators.note: the word for territory forms a border round the other letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: land is territory

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word pole are used

explanation.surface: A region next to one of the Earth's poles, described with a question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pole' reads as a Polish person, but 'oddly' takes letters from the word. The whole clue also describes the region, which lies in the far north towards the North Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic region of the Sami people spans northern Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia, reaching towards the North Pole.

clue.text: Continually blocking grant to youngster in form

indicators.note: one word sitting inside another blocks it, so the word for continually goes into the middle

parts.note: to let is to grant or allow
ever, as in 'ever hopeful', means always

explanation.surface: Something constantly getting in the way of a grant meant for a young person in a school form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' looks like a school class, but a hare's resting place is called its form.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare, and a hare's nest or lair is known as its form.

clue.text: Fish cut up with great force

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' tells you to write the word for cut from bottom to top

parts.note: to clip is to cut
hard, as in 'hit hard'

explanation.surface: A fish being chopped up violently.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish related to the herring, the adult sardine.

clue.text: Analyse a singular state

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
to say is to state

explanation.surface: An instruction to study one particular state, perhaps of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To test or examine a metal or substance chemically to find its composition.

clue.text: Doctor gets our compound — here in US, perhaps

indicators.note: to compound is to mix ingredients together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician makes up a compound, which in America would happen in a certain shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a noun the doctor makes, but it is the signal to mix GETS OUR into UGSTORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An American pharmacy or chemist's shop, where a compound might be made up.

clue.text: Barren wife deputising for husband in expedition

indicators.note: one letter standing in for another, as a deputy stands in, signals a swap

parts.note: expedition in its old sense of speed means haste

explanation.surface: An infertile wife takes her husband's place on a journey of exploration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' suggests a trip, but here it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land is waste ground, uncultivated and desolate.

clue.text: Thrillers incorporating papers women left behind

indicators.note: one word takes another into its body, so the word for papers sits inside

parts.note: wows are sensations that thrill an audience
ID, short for identification, means identity papers

explanation.surface: Crime novels that involve documents left behind by some women.
explanation.definitionFit: Women whose husbands have died, leaving them behind.

clue.text: Apprehension from last character that is returning to crack safe

indicators.note: cracking open a word lets another into its middle

parts.note: sure, as in 'a safe bet', means certain

indicators.note: the letters are written in reverse order, coming back the way they went

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A thief's anxiety about the last thing needed to break into a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprehension' looks like worry, but it is the act of arresting or seizing.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension in the sense of arrest: taking hold of a person or goods by force.

clue.text: Leave old mate with distress

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to eat, as in 'what's eating you?', is to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: Abandon a former friend with grief.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is permission for a pupil to be away from a British boarding school or college.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal permission for absence, the noun sense of leave as in 'shore leave'.

clue.text: Why a note goes astray in transit?

indicators.note: letters that wander off course end up in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking why a letter in the post gets lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling and not yet arrived, as a parcel is while being delivered.

clue.text: Marine vehicle driven to port by a learner

indicators.note: port is the left side, so in an across clue the word travels leftwards, read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A seaborne vehicle being driven into harbour by a learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine and naval both describe things belonging to the sea or a navy.

clue.text: Spooner's secured location, in a few words

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so two words here trade their first letters

parts.note: bound means tied down or secured
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Describing a secure place briefly, in the manner of the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A short extracted quote or phrase, a few words used by the media.

clue.text: Yankee on drug adopting Republican line, roughly

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it
taking something in, as a family adopts a child, places it inside

parts.note: hash is short for hashish, a drug
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American on drugs taking up the Republican party line, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' looks like 'approximately', but it is the definition: in a rough way.
explanation.definitionFit: Done harshly means done in a rough, severe manner.

clue.text: Went out with clean 5 across from timberyard

parts.note: saw, as in 'they saw each other for a year', means dated
to dust is to clean

explanation.surface: Someone dated a woman with a clean, barren rubbish dump from a timber merchant's yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is WASTE: the definition is waste from a timberyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine particles left over when wood is cut, the leftover by-product of a sawmill.

clue.text: Mac's strength of spirit added to general excellence

definitions.note: read as 'Mac is', a mac being a raincoat; the noun defines the answer

indicators.note: one piece is attached after another

parts.note: water is the quality of a diamond, hence 'of the first water', of highest excellence
proof measures the alcoholic strength of a spirit

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's courage reckoned on top of his all-round excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' suggests a Scot, but it is a mackintosh, a raincoat; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a raincoat, a rain-resistant garment or coat.

clue.text: Mentioning task for second examiner?

definitions.meaning: a second examiner marks a paper again

explanation.surface: Talking about the job given to an exam's second marker.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in passing; and marking an exam script a second time.

clue.text: Charge double, initially, for forage

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Billing twice over for animal fodder, at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search for food, to feed as grazing animals do.

clue.text: Puts down free oyster cards, taking car out

indicators.note: letters set free are released to settle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller discards free London travel cards and drives instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking car out' removes C, A, R from the letters of OYSTER CARDS; the rest rearrange. An Oyster card is a London transport smartcard.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down an animal is to destroy or kill it humanely.

clue.text: Momentous contest well-nigh complete

parts.note: an event is a competition or contest

indicators.note: almost, so the word for complete loses its final letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A significant match that is very nearly over.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of important happenings, synonym of momentous.

clue.text: Sort of tale that'll keep you in stitches?

definitions.meaning: a long rambling story, as in 'spin a ...'
wool for knitting, the stitches being knitted rather than laughter

explanation.surface: A funny story that will have you laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: A long story, and spun thread used to knit stitches.

clue.text: Wild rave a politician's caught in

indicators.note: the politician and article are trapped within the word for rave

parts.note: to rant is to rave
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A political figure gets trapped at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave' tempts as a party, but it is a verb meaning rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means unrestrained, flourishing out of control, so wild.

clue.text: Victor commanding guards, impossible to pass

indicators.note: the word for commanding wraps around and guards the letter

parts.note: imperious means domineering, commanding
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A military commander's guards are impenetrable.
explanation.definitionFit: Not allowing anything to pass through; impenetrable.

clue.text: Against crew changing direction without a second glance?

parts.note: on, as in leaning on, means resting against

indicators.note: a compass point is swapped for another, east becoming south

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: Turning a rowing crew around to face the other way, with barely a look.
explanation.walkthrough: E (east) in EIGHT becomes S (south), giving SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Done immediately upon seeing, with no time for a second look.

clue.text: Courageous chap's end providential

indicators.note: the end of the word chap means only its final letter is used

parts.note: lucky, fortunate

explanation.surface: A brave man's death was fortunate.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means brave, having pluck or courage.

clue.text: Better medic with peculiarly regal bearing

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the rearranged word carries the letters inside it
strangely, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A superior doctor who has an oddly majestic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like 'superior', but it means one who bets. REGAL rearranged gives GALER, with MB inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A better (bettor) is one who bets, synonym of punter.

clue.text: Raised e-cigarette's casing following blunder

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word writes it upwards
the e-cigarette letters wrap around the abbreviation for following

parts.note: taken as written
fag is British slang for a cigarette
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A vaper's device held up after a social slip.
explanation.walkthrough: E + FAG casing F gives EFFAG, which written upwards makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: House maybe trades gold

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A house perhaps swaps for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a royal house: the British royal family's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The current British royal dynasty, an example of a royal house.

clue.text: Energy-filled, unrestrained exercise

indicators.note: the word for unrestrained is filled with the letter, which goes inside

parts.note: wild means uncontrolled
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Lively, unrestrained physical exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise power or influence is to wield it.

clue.text: Concession that man's pocketed in republic

indicators.note: something pocketed is put inside, so the words go into the middle

parts.note: France is a republic
his means belonging to that man

explanation.surface: A man's concession has been pocketed in a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a concession or licence granted to trade.

clue.text: Return of goods — deficiency ultimately unclear

indicators.note: the little word is written back to front

parts.note: G is short for good, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: only the last letter of deficiency is taken

explanation.surface: A refund of goods with a defect is not clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Foggy means hazy, muddled, so unclear.

clue.text: Tail-enders in the marathon put a strain on all runners

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: to try, as in trying one's patience, is to strain it

explanation.surface: Slow finishers in a marathon wear out everyone running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are the entrants in a race, not athletes being strained.
explanation.definitionFit: The entry of a race is the whole field of competitors.

clue.text: Crowd on balcony when faithful audience is catered for

definitions.text: when faithful audience is catered for

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: the gods are the highest balcony in a theatre
a lot is a crowd or group

explanation.surface: A crowd on a theatre balcony as a devoted audience is served.
explanation.walkthrough: A god slot is a British TV or radio time set aside for religious programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting period reserved for religious programmes, serving believers in the audience.
